title: Retrying failed webhooks
summary: Webhook deliveries used to be sent once, inline, from the billing API. Now the API writes each event to an outbox table in the same transaction as the billing change, and a separate worker delivers it, retrying with growing delays and giving up into a dead-letter queue. Receivers can tell a retry from a new event and can verify it really came from us.

concepts.name: Transactional outbox
concepts.explanation: Write the message you need to send into a table in the same database transaction as the business change. A separate process sends it later. Either both happen or neither does, so you never charge someone without telling them.
concepts.whyHere: The plan change and its webhook event are committed together; delivery moved out of the request.

concepts.name: Exponential backoff
concepts.explanation: Wait longer after each failure, doubling the delay each time (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s…), so a struggling server gets room to recover instead of more traffic.
concepts.whyHere: Each failed delivery is rescheduled at base × 2^attempt, capped at one hour.

concepts.name: Jitter
concepts.explanation: Add randomness to each wait, so clients that failed together don't all retry at the same instant.
concepts.whyHere: The delay is picked at random between 0 and the backoff value (full jitter).

concepts.name: Idempotency keys
concepts.explanation: A unique ID sent with a request so the receiver can recognise a repeat and skip doing the work twice.
concepts.whyHere: Retries are now normal, so every delivery carries the event ID as Idempotency-Key.

concepts.name: Dead-letter queue
concepts.explanation: Where messages go after they keep failing: they stop retrying forever but aren't lost, and someone can inspect and replay them.
concepts.whyHere: After 8 attempts a delivery moves to dead letters for manual replay.

concepts.name: HMAC signatures
concepts.explanation: A hash of the message made with a shared secret. The receiver recomputes it to prove the message came from you and wasn't altered.
concepts.whyHere: Payloads are signed with SHA-256 HMAC plus a timestamp so receivers can reject forged or replayed webhooks.
